allowed_changes: use only S&P 500 as the economic risk asset
post-close state is 100% S&P 500 for execution dates whose calendar month is November through April and 100% CashYieldCNY for May through October
state changes only when the fixed calendar state changes at the first observed May or November session
one full-period S&P 500 buy-and-hold control and one CNY cash control
use product-level 1.00% fee plus 0.05% slippage with no sensitivity grid
expected_outputs: Halloween, S&P500 buy-hold and CNY cash portfolio CSVs
trade count, active session count, average cash, realized max gross, minimum cash and target fingerprint
global post-protocol DSR after formal run
run authorization, execution commit and SHA artifact manifest
follow_up_policy: After any formal performance metric is viewed, do not shift calendar months, entry/exit session, asset, cost, or add any filter in this lineage. Alternative seasonal windows are forbidden rescue variants, not follow-ups.
forbidden_changes: October, December or turn-of-month shifted entry/exit dates
different summer/winter month windows or optimizing entry/exit days
Nasdaq, Russell, sector, China or gold substitution after results
using the engine-support Nasdaq series as an economic target
trend, momentum, VIX, volatility, macro, weekday, election, holiday or January filters
shorting, leverage, financing, gross exposure above 100% or negative cash
hypothesis: The documented Halloween effect proposes that broad equity returns are concentrated in the November-April half-year. A fixed, no-signal implementation that holds S&P 500 from the close of the first observed November session until the close of the first observed May session, and CNY demand cash otherwise, may retain a persistent seasonal equity premium while cutting approximately half of annual equity exposure and keeping product-level turnover to roughly two state changes per year.
pass_fail_gates: at least 70% of seven fixed folds have Sharpe >0
max realized gross <=100% and minimum cash >=0
research_basis: Bouman & Jacobsen, The Halloween Indicator, Sell in May and Go Away: Another Puzzle, American Economic Review 2002; higher November-April returns across most studied markets

Dichtl & Drobetz, Sell in May and Go Away: Still Good Advice for Investors? 2014; post-publication/investable-period evidence suggests the effect weakened or diminished, motivating a strict contemporary replication rather than assuming persistence
selection_metric: No month search. Exactly one canonical November-April equity / May-October cash calendar rule. Validation, objective and buy-hold comparison are independent ATM-SVP-3 axes.
strategy_lineage: halloween-001 / Sell-in-May 001; fixed half-year S&P500 calendar seasonality
swift_engine_entrypoint: scripts/run_halloween_001.py -> tools/halloween_001.swiftpart + tools/halloween_001_logic.swift -> BacktestEngine.runResearchTargetProviderStrategyWithTrace; Nasdaq input is engine alignment support only and never receives target weight
validation_gates: base run already includes product-level cost; missing a second stress is reported as a warning
